features.name: Create, edit, and persist a normal note
steps: Tap + in the bottom-right corner
Choose "new note"
Enter the title and body
Return to the note list
The new note appears in the list
After reopening the title and body are preserved
Modify the content and exit again
The updated content continues to be saved. Temporary text must not be maintained only on the current page.
features.expected: A new note must be genuinely saved and appear in the list; the title and body are preserved after exiting and re-entering; after successive edits the latest content is saved; temporary text must not be maintained only on the current page.

features.name: Create and manage to-do notes
steps: "Create to-do"
Enter the title and body
A checkbox appears in the list after saving
Tap the checkbox to mark it complete
Tap again to restore it to incomplete
After opening the to-do the original body is still preserved. A normal note can also be converted to a to-do via the menu, and a to-do can be converted back to a normal note.
features.expected: To-dos must show a checkbox with a toggleable, persistent completion state; the completed and incomplete states are consistent with the list display; converting between a normal note and a to-do does not lose the body content.

features.name: To-do sorting and completion-state filtering
steps: Create several completed/incomplete to-dos
Open the list filter
Toggle "hide completed"
Completed items disappear from the list but their data is not deleted
After changing settings such as "pin incomplete to-dos" the list order is recomputed
After restoring the filter the items reappear.
features.expected: Hiding completed only affects the display without deleting data; after changing settings such as pinning incomplete to-dos the list order is recomputed; after restoring the filter the completed items reappear with unchanged states.

features.name: Notebook creation and note assignment
steps: Enter the notebook system from the sidebar
Create a new notebook
Create a note in that notebook
Check the full list and that notebook's list separately
Use Reveal in notebook from the note menu to locate the containing notebook. A real parent-child relationship between notebooks and notes is required.
features.expected: Notebooks and notes must have a real parent-child relationship; notes are correctly assigned and the locate feature points to the containing notebook; deleting a notebook must handle its notes consistently without losing data.

features.name: Tag management
steps: Open a note
Use tag operations
Add or choose a tag
The tag relationships are preserved after returning
Re-entering the tag editor shows the associated tags
After removing the tag the relations update in sync. If several notes use the same tag they should share the same tag entity rather than generating duplicate text.
features.expected: A tag is a shared entity: several notes using the same tag must not produce duplicates; after removing the tag the associations update in sync; the tag count matches the actual number of associated notes.

features.name: Full-text search
steps: Create several notes whose titles and bodies contain different keywords
Tap search
Enter keywords
Return the matching notes
Tapping a result opens the correct note
Search again after modifying the note so the keyword disappears
The results update with the data. Both title and body searches should work.
features.expected: Both the title and body can be matched by search; tapping a result opens the correct note; after modifying the note so the keyword disappears, searching again no longer returns it; an empty state is shown when there are no matches.

features.name: Note-list sorting
steps: Create several notes with different titles, creation times, and update times
Open sorting/filtering
Switch between the sort modes shown in the screenshot such as "update time, creation date, title, custom order, due date, completion date"
Then toggle ascending/descending again
The list order changes accordingly immediately.
features.expected: Each sort mode immediately changes the list order with ascending and descending giving opposite results; the sort state is preserved; the custom order can be adjusted by dragging and persists.

features.name: Markdown headings and basic text formats
steps: Enter text in the Markdown editor
Use the H1/H2/H3/H4/H5, bold, and italic tools
The corresponding Markdown structure is inserted or directly rendered as formatting
After switching to view mode different heading levels, bold, and italic are displayed
Returning to edit mode, the content can still be modified.
features.expected: Toolbar operations must insert the correct Markdown structure or apply the format directly; view mode renders headings, bold, and italic hierarchically; editing and viewing show the same content.

features.name: Code and math formulas
steps: Enter plain text
Use the "code" tool to wrap text or insert a code structure
Use the "math" tool to insert a mathematical expression
View mode correctly distinguishes plain text, code, and math formulas
The rendered result changes in sync after the source content is modified.
features.expected: Code and math formulas render in the corresponding styles in view mode without ordinary text being misinterpreted; the rendered result changes in sync after the source content is modified; the raw text is always preserved.

features.name: Ordered, unordered, and task lists
steps: Enter multi-line text
Use "ordered list", "unordered list", and "task list" respectively
The line start converts to the corresponding structure
Task-list checkboxes can be checked
Use "Increase indent level/Decrease indent level" to form nested lists
The hierarchy and checkbox structure are preserved when returning to view mode.
features.expected: The three list structures insert the corresponding syntax; task-list checkboxes can be checked with the state persisted; indentation forms nested levels; view mode preserves the hierarchy and checkbox structure.

features.name: Advanced row operations in the editor
steps: Create multi-line content in the body
Select/locate a row
Use "Swap row up", "Swap row down", "Delete row", and "Duplicate row in place"
The text structure changes immediately
Select several rows and use "sort selected rows"
Only the selected area is sorted
Use "Go to start/end of note" to jump to the start or end of the note.
features.expected: Swap, delete, and duplicate row operations only affect the target row; sorting the selected rows only affects the selected area; jumping to the start or end of the document places the cursor correctly; the operation results persist after saving.

features.name: Markdown toolbar customization
steps: Open "manage toolbar options"
Remove an existing button
The button disappears after returning to the editor
Then re-enable H1/H3/H4/H5 or the advanced row operations
The button joins the toolbar
Use the up/down arrows to adjust the button order
Return to the editor to verify the actual order changed.
features.expected: After removing a button it disappears from the editor toolbar; enabling it brings the button back; the order adjusted with the up/down arrows matches the editor's actual order; the configuration persists.

features.name: Real-time Markdown format rendering
steps: Enable "render markup in the editor" in the settings
Enter Markdown such as headings, bold, italic, and links
Some formats are visually rendered without leaving the editing page while remaining editable
Closing the setting restores a display closer to the raw Markdown.
features.expected: When enabled the editor immediately renders headings, bold, and other formats while the text stays editable; when disabled the raw Markdown display returns; toggling does not modify the note's actual content.

features.name: Inline Markdown image rendering
steps: Insert an image attachment into the note
Enable "Markdown editor: render images"
The image is displayed at the corresponding position in the Markdown editing area
After disabling that item it returns to the resource/Markdown representation
The image resource itself must not be lost.
features.expected: When enabled the image is displayed at the corresponding position in the editing area; when disabled it returns to the Markdown syntax display; the image resource itself must not be lost.

features.name: Switch between view mode and edit mode
steps: Create a Markdown note with headings, lists, links, and images
Modify the source text in the editing state
Switch to View mode
Show the fully rendered result that is not directly editable
Then switch back to editing
The raw Markdown content still exists with a reasonable cursor/data state.
features.expected: View mode renders the complete result and is not directly editable; switching back to edit mode fully preserves the raw Markdown content; switching does not duplicate or lose content.

features.name: Rich-text editing toggle
steps: Choose "edit as rich text" from the note menu
Markdown content is converted into a rich-text presentation
Make visible edits to the text
Save and return

Reopen the note and the modification is still there; when switching between the rich-text and Markdown representations the basic structures such as headings, bold, lists, and links should stay consistent.
features.expected: After conversion the structures such as headings, bold, lists, and links stay consistent; changes made in rich text persist after saving and reopening; switching back and forth between the two representations must not damage the content.

features.name: Links and internal note links
steps: Use the "link" tool in the editor to add a URL
View mode shows clickable links; use "copy Markdown link" on a note
Paste that link into another note
Tapping jumps to the target note. "Copy external link address" in the menu should produce a corresponding copyable address.
features.expected: URLs display as clickable links in view mode; copying a Markdown link and pasting it into another note allows jumping to the target note; copying an external link produces a usable external address.

features.name: File, image, audio-recording, and drawing attachments
steps: Create/edit a note
Use the "attachment, audio recording, camera, drawing" entries respectively via the + menu
Generate or select the resource
The resource is associated with the current note
After returning and reopening the note the resource still exists
Images can be displayed, and supported audio/video can present the corresponding media entry in the note.
features.expected: Attachments must be genuinely saved and bound to the note; they can still be seen and accessed after exiting and re-entering; images can be displayed and audio/video provide a media entry; deleting a note must handle the attachments consistently.

features.name: Note reminders
steps: Set the note as a to-do
Choose "set reminder" from the menu
SET DATE sets the date and time
Save the reminder
The reminder information still exists after exiting and reopening
The system notification triggers at the specified time
After re-entering the settings and choosing "clear reminder" it no longer triggers.
features.expected: The reminder time persists after saving and reopening; the system notification triggers at the time; after clearing the reminder it no longer triggers; to-dos and normal notes behave consistently for reminders.

features.name: Note properties and metadata
steps: Create and modify a note
Open "note properties"
Show the creation time and update time
After modifying the body the update time changes while the creation time is preserved
If the note has saved location data, "view on map" opens the corresponding location behavior.
features.expected: After modifying the body the update time changes while the creation time keeps its original value; the property data matches the actual note; when location data exists, viewing it on the map opens the corresponding location.

features.name: Note version history
steps: Create note content A
Save and continue modifying to B/C
Produce history records with note history enabled
Open the "version history" entry to view the old state
The current note and the old version data need to be distinguishable; the history-retention configuration should affect how long old versions are ultimately kept.
features.expected: Modifying a note produces a history record and the old version content differs from the current one; old states can be viewed; the history-retention setting affects how long old versions are ultimately kept.

features.name: Deletion, recycle bin, and lifecycle
steps: Create a note
Menu "delete"
The note disappears from the normal list and enters the recycle bin
Items in the recycle bin are still identifiable
Final cleanup follows the configured retention days; the "automatically delete notes from the recycle bin after N days" toggle and the day count need to affect the actual data lifecycle.
features.expected: After deletion the note disappears from the normal list and enters the recycle bin; recycle-bin items are still identifiable and recoverable; the retention days and auto-delete toggles genuinely affect the data lifecycle.

features.name: Markdown extension rendering toggles
steps: In the Markdown settings, test each extension shown in the screenshot one by one: soft line breaks, Typographer, Linkify, math expressions, Fountain, Mermaid diagrams, ABC music notation, audio player, video player, ==mark== highlight, footnotes, table-of-contents extension, and ~sub~ subscript. Prepare a minimal example for each feature
After enabling the toggle, the corresponding rendering appears in view mode
After disabling it is no longer interpreted by that extension while the raw text is still saved.
features.expected: After enabling each extension toggle the corresponding syntax renders correctly in view mode, and after disabling it is no longer interpreted by that extension; the raw text is always preserved; the extensions do not interfere with one another.

features.name: Settings persist and take effect across screens
steps: Modify the user settings already visible in the screenshot: language, date format, time format, light/dark theme, viewer font size, editor font size/font, spell check, Markdown toolbar, default view/edit state, large-image scaling policy, whether to save geolocation, etc.
Leave the settings page and re-enter
The settings are preserved
Return to the related pages to confirm the real behavior changes with the configuration.
features.expected: All modified settings are preserved after leaving and re-entering; the theme, font size, etc. genuinely affect the corresponding screens; the settings are not lost after restarting the app and do not override one another.
